root_cause.text: In EROFS file-backed mounts, `erofs_fileio_ki_complete()` treated short reads at end-of-file as a successful completion without properly zero-filling the remaining BIO data, so I/O past the filesystem end could return stale/uninitialized data instead of zeroes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the completion path from only zero-filling when `ret > 0` to zero-filling whenever `ret >= 0 && ret != rq->bio.bi_iter.bi_size`, and the commit message explicitly states that “I/O requests beyond the end of the filesystem should be zeroed out,” fixing the fileio path introduced by `ce63cb62d794 ("erofs: support unencoded inodes for fileio")`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix file I/O completion handling so partial successes are zero-filled correctly and error propagation is routed appropriately based on whether a bio end I/O handler is present.
intent_record.what: In `erofs_fileio_ki_complete()`, the completion logic was reordered and simplified: the partial-success handling now runs for any non-negative `ret` that is not equal to the bio size, the code that iterates folios is moved under `if (!rq->bio.bi_end_io)`, the `erofs_onlinefolio_end()` call now receives a boolean `ret < 0` instead of the raw `ret` value, and the block-status assignment for negative errors is now in the `else if` branch when `bi_end_io` exists.
intent_record.how: At runtime, successful short reads/writes now still trigger bio advancement and zero-filling, while error reporting to folio completion is converted from passing a raw return code to a simple failure flag. If the bio has its own `bi_end_io`, the code now only propagates an error status there and avoids the folio iteration path, preventing incorrect completion semantics and making partial completion handling consistent for non-error cases.

intent_record.intent_summary: Change ret to ssize_t in erofs file I/O submission to correctly represent I/O return values.
intent_record.what: In erofs_fileio_rq_submit(), the type of the local variable ret was changed from int to ssize_t; no other code in the function was modified.
intent_record.how: This allows the function to store and handle return values using the signed size type typically used for I/O operations, avoiding type narrowing or mismatch when dealing with potentially large byte counts or negative error codes.

Change ret to ssize_t in erofs file I/O submission to correctly represent I/O return values.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes file I/O completion for partial/short reads by zero-filling remaining BIO data and adjusting completion/error handling, which addresses stale data exposure past EOF.

The change only adjusts the type of a return variable in EROFS file I/O submission. It does not address the EOF short-read handling or the missing zero-fill behavior in erofs_fileio_ki_complete() that caused stale data to be returned.

candidates.rationale: This is the completion path that incorrectly treats any positive short read as success; in the vulnerable code path, end-of-file short reads could be finalized without ensuring the remaining BIO range was zero-filled.
This condition detects partial completion, but the bug is that the subsequent handling did not reliably cover EOF short reads with proper zero-filling semantics for all remaining BIO data.

For a short successful read, this converts the result into success, which is the vulnerable behavior when the remaining data beyond EOF has not been zero-filled and may leak stale/uninitialized bytes.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line turns any short successful read into a full success result. In the vulnerable EOF path, that allowed the completion handler to finalize without ensuring the unread portion of the BIO was zero-filled, enabling stale or uninitialized data to be returned.

This partial-completion check is part of the flawed completion logic. It leads into handling that incorrectly treats EOF short reads as successful completion instead of ensuring the remaining BIO range is zero-filled.
This branch accepts any positive short read as a success path. In the vulnerable code, that permitted end-of-file reads to be completed without properly zero-filling the remaining BIO data.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this file. In this commit, short-read handling happens in `erofs_fileio_ki_complete()`: `if (ret > 0) { if (ret != rq->bio.bi_iter.bi_size) { bio_advance(&rq->bio, ret); zero_fill_bio(&rq->bio); } ret = 0; }`. This explicitly advances past the bytes already read and calls `zero_fill_bio()` on the remainder, which is the correct handling for EOF-short reads. Because the code already zero-fills the unread portion, the stale/uninitialized data bug is absent here. The snippet is sufficient to make this determination because the relevant completion logic is shown directly.
